definition: Environmentalism means the movement dedicated to protecting the natural world.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word environmentalism. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know environmentalism should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Her environmentalism lives in small habits — the bike commute, the rain barrels, the patient letters to the water board.
Appreciation asks nothing of you — loving the view from the trail stops far short of environmentalism.
Conservation goes further than appreciation but stops short of environmentalism: it stewards particular places and stocks, while the -ism presses to change laws, budgets, and habits everywhere.

Ecology is the science of how living things interact with each other and their surroundings — coursework, field data, peer review. Environmentalism is not a science but a cause: the organized movement pressing laws, budgets, and habits into the natural world's defense. One is studied; the other is fought for.

Stewardship is the quiet ethic of taking care of what is in your charge — a farm kept healthy, a trust kept whole — answerable mostly to your own conscience. Environmentalism is public and organized: a movement that recruits, campaigns, and legislates far beyond any one person's plot.
